definitions.gloss: densely; lushly; thickly (of trees or vegetation)
definitions.explanation: Describes vegetation growing thickly enough to block out light and create a shadowy atmosphere. Almost always paired with verbs of growing or covering.

examples.japanese: {木|き}がうっそうと{茂|しげ}る。
うっそうとした{森|もり}を{歩|ある}いた。
examples.english: I walked through a thickly wooded forest.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{神社|じんじゃ}の{周|まわ}りには、うっそうとした{杉|すぎ}の{木|き}が{何百年|なんびゃくねん}も{立|た}ち{続|つづ}けていた。
examples.english: Around the old shrine, dense cedars had stood for hundreds of years.

notes:
Sometimes written {鬱蒼|うっそう}と in formal text but more commonly in kana. Often carries a slightly gloomy or atmospheric nuance — the density blocks light.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- うっそうと{茂|しげ}る: grow densely
- うっそうとした{森|もり}: thickly wooded forest
- うっそうとした{木立|こだち}: dense grove
- うっそうと{生|お}い{茂|しげ}る: grow thickly and lushly

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {青々|あおあお}と: vivid green — emphasizes color, not density
- もこもこ: bushy; fluffy — visual texture, not specifically vegetation
- {鬱蒼|うっそう}たる: same meaning, more literary/formal form
